title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks extended their slide Friday — Nasdaq -5.3% (worst week in over a year, now red for 2026), S&P 500 -3.7%, Dow -949pts (-1.9%); S&P and Dow are both down >10% from recent highs, in correction territory, as AI-buildout jitters deepened.

Markets: Treasuries rallied as yields plunged — the 10-year fell to 4.909% (-0.14pt Friday, -0.24pt on the week) and the 2-year posted its biggest weekly drop since 2024; gold fell 4.6% to $3,512/oz (fresh 52-week lows) and Brent crude ended the week down 3.4% (~$92.57/bbl). Chipmakers were hit hardest, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index down ~11% on the day.

Companies: Anthropic's IPO — the largest on record at $93.5B raised and a ~$1.7T valuation (briefly topping Meta) — reversed hard on day two, falling as much as 12% to near its $83 listing price after a 17% first-day pop, as employees began selling into the broader tech rout.

Companies: Meta disclosed a 45% jump in AI-driven data-center emissions and is reconsidering its 2030 net-zero target; Nvidia was subpoenaed by California's AG over a probe into CEO conduct, AI-chip claims and its China dealings.
Macro/Policy: The White House named Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies as the new national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross amid a broader shakeup of Trump's AI/tech team.

Macro/Policy: Traders are pricing in near-certainty of another Fed rate move in December as growth and AI-spending concerns weigh on the outlook; next week's data focus shifts to the PCE inflation report, new home sales, Case-Shiller home prices, and earnings from Dell, Best Buy, Dollar Tree and Deere.
